description: init.sh creates .venv, installs driftpatch with dev tools, lints and runs every test offline
Acme Orders spec v1 and v2, a Python client and a TypeScript client whose own tests pass against a mock of v1
The built-in differ finds removed endpoints, renamed fields, removed fields, new required parameters, changed types and changed enums
The oasdiff adapter runs oasdiff when installed (external refs off), maps its ids to kinds, and the tool runs without it
The Python call-site finder (ast) scopes each change to the functions that call the affected endpoint
The TypeScript call-site finder (patterns and a brace scanner), marked weaker in the README
A mock server built from a spec on 127.0.0.1 that validates requests and answers with examples
The verifier runs the client tests before and after a patch in a temp copy with timeouts and applies the pass rule
The rule-based proposer handles renames, new required parameters with a default and removed fields, and declines the rest
The pipeline is an explicit state machine (diff, find, propose, verify, report) and every transition is tested
A frozen suite of 30 to 40 cases with known correct patches, a SHA-256 manifest test and a 25 dev / rest held-out split
The benchmark runs end to end in under 10 minutes on 2 cores with the rule-based proposer
A test proves the tool never runs git push and connects only to the local mock server or the configured model endpoint, and the guard blocks planted bad calls
The pluggable LLM proposer works in replay mode from recorded fixtures and refuses unsafe answers
One record-mode run of the LLM proposer on a free provider over the suite, with token counts
blocked: record mode blocked: model hosts answer 403 through the proxy and no key is set (BLOCKERS.md). The LLM row is 'not run'.

description: The census counts breaking changes by kind across the Stripe and GitHub spec histories and documents the method
run writes a unified diff, a plain-English PR text and a verification report, and never pushes or opens a PR
README tables (pass rate, regressions, patch size, tokens per proposer, 95% intervals) are written from results files and a test checks them
Quality bar: README parts in order, LICENSE, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, issue templates, CI with badge, topics, social preview, static demo page and DEMO.md
Study-later kit: WALKTHROUGH, INTERVIEW_QA with the four interview points, DECISIONS
Release check done: code review, security audit, gitleaks, pip-audit, ruff S, actionlint, link check, humanizer pass, outside check
Hand-off: CHANGELOG v0.1.0-rc1 with the release SHA, HUMAN_STEPS, GITHUB_ABOUT and topics
